text: An important statement in regard to the anti-British strike and boycott in Canton was made in the House of Commons by Sir Austen Chamberlain, who referred to the recent negotiations for a settlement; expressed his admiration for the resource and courage of the British communities of Hongkong, Canton, and Swatow; explained why it is not advisable to despatch a Special Commissioner to Canton; and asserted that he was still giving the whole question his closest consideration.

label: text
text: Sir Austen Chamberlain, Foreign Secretary, made a statement on the situation in China in the House of Commons today. He said that His Majesty's Government was giving careful and constant attention to the serious problem arising out of the anti-British strike and boycott in Southern China. At the beginning of the year it seemed likely that the negotiations between Hongkong and Canton would be successful. They had, unfortunately, broken down in a manner which must make it clear to the rest of China and, indeed, to the whole world that the Government of Canton was for the time being under influences so blindly anti-British that they were not open to reasonable settlement.

label: text
text:
Our Friendly Policy.
The position in the rest of China was different. The policy of the British Government, having been dictated by a sincere desire to promote friendly relations with the Chinese people, and being inspired by their legitimate aspirations, this attitude of patience and conciliation was bearing fruit in the slow but steady restoration of friendship and good will between the British and Chinese peoples. The trade conditions in the Yangtse Valley were now improving, and would be equally improving in North China if it were not for civil war, whilst order was being re-established.

label: text
text: There were many signs that these lawless actions were directly attributable to Communistic activities, which had disgusted all sections of the Chinese people, who were very far from approving the actions of the extremist section in Canton. This, feeling would doubtless spread, unless the intervention of the foreign Powers strengthened the extremists and thus united China against the aggressives.

label: text
text:
Hongkong Prised.
“Meanwhile,” Sir Austen Chamberlain continued, “I must be allowed to express my admiration for the resource and courage with which the British Colony of Hongkong and the British communities of Canton and Swatow have faced so serious a situation. The whole question has recently been examined and now and most carefully by the Foreign Office in conjunction with our representatives in China, and I shall continue to give it my closest attention.”

label: text
text: Replying to Mr. F. W. Pethick-Lawrence (Labour, Leicester), Sir Austen Chamberlain, after referring to the Chinese authorities' refusal to accept the cheque for compensation in respect of the incidents in Shanghai last May, said he hoped that the policy of patient conciliation, steadily followed by the British Government, was tending gradually to remove the ill-feeling caused by those incidents and to restore good will between the British and Chinese peoples. He added that he did not regret that the matter was referred to a judicial authority, which had substantiated our decision to make the facts known.

label: text
text: Replying to Commander John Kenworthy (Liberal, Hull Central), Sir Austen Chamberlain said he had no official information as to whether any Britons were serving in Chan Kwingming's army. He referred the questioner to Article 75 of the China Order in Council, 1925 regarding participation on either side which, he said, was being strictly enforced.

text: The s.s. "Franconia," one of the Cunard Fleet, is due to arrive at Hongkong on March 21, on her third cruise-de-luxe round the world. The cruise commenced from New York on January 14, and in her circuit of the globe a call is made at the following places: Funchal, Gibraltar, Monaco, Naples, Athens, Alexandria, Port Said, Bombay, Colombo, Padang, Batavia, Singapore, Manila, Hongkong, Shanghai, Chin Wang Tao, Yokohama, Honolulu, Hilo, San Francisco, San Pedro, Balboa, Christobal, and Havana, thence to New York. The ottal distance covered will be over 30,000 miles extending over four and a half months.

label: text
text: The "Franconia," which has been specially designed for world cruising, is over 600 feet long and has a gross tonnage of 20,000. Her accommodation, which allows the very highest degree of luxury, includes many distinctive "features." For instance she possesses a wonderful sporting arena. It includes a gymnasium fully equipped not only with the ordinary apparatus for physical culture but with a host of mechanical electric devices such as can only be found in the highest type of physical culture schools on shores. There is a large swimming pool and a rackets court. In addition there is an extensive sun deck where all manner of sports can be held in the open air. Her public rooms include a card room, writing room, garden lounge, drawing room, smoking room, and a magnificent dining saloon. In addition to superb staterooms, the "Franconia" also has a number of private suites and excellent en suites with private baths.

text: The activities of the white ants who have dared to interfere with the smooth working of the administration of justice in the Supreme Court are to be effectively checked.

label: text
text: For some months the three huge circles of electric bulbs suspended from the ceiling have given a certain amount of trouble. It has only needed the vibration from a passing tram or car, or a passer by in the corridor, for them so far to forget themselves as to wink simultaneously.

label: text
text: For such contempt of court they were marked down for attention but it has not hitherto been possible to get on which the work owing to pressure of court work. As the Supreme Court has now no sitting until the 22nd., advantage being taken of the interval, scaffolding having been erected in the court and a dozen or more workmen are engaged in the work.

label: text
text: It was discovered that the industry of the white ants had led to the inconvenience to which the court was put, an important connection having been rendered imperfect and inoperative when subject to vibration.

label: text
text: About 1.30 this morning the local ferry steam launch "Lee Fat" sank, close to the Praya, a little beyond the Wing Lok (Macao steamer) wharf, but no life was lost.

label: text
text:
Recently the launch had been on the ferry service between Hongkong and Deep Day (Hau Hoi). She returned yesterday about noon and should have left again at 5 a.m. to day.
While secured by rope (to the bow) to the Praya wall last night, the coxswain was awakened by the crew to find water rushing in over the stern. It is believed that the wind carried the launch towards the seawall with the result that the bow was lifted up through touching ground, while the stern receded into the harbour.

label: text
text: There was a pronounced list to port. The coxswain ordered the bunker coal to be shifted to star board. When this was being done, the launch listed over to starboard and sank. The crew were rescued.

label: text
text: When a report was made this morning the launch was still secured by a rope, but was mostl under water.

label: text
text: Some months ago the "Lee Fat" was on the service to Cheung Chau (Dumbell Island) when she was pirated.

label: text
text: The fun of the fair was at its height yesterday in the case of a Chinese who was busy raking in the coppers with a novel form of price game in which cigarettes and sweetts were given away as prizes. A dettitive who was baffled by the man's good look made a close investigation of the table and found a secret spring which enabled him to stop the revolving disc at any desired point.

label: text
text: With a smile on his face, the man informed the Magistrate this morning that he was only having a bit of fun. The Magistrate agreed that it was a delightful game, but said that he could not regard him as a public benefactor. A fine of $2 was imposed for keeping a gaming table.

label: text
text: The Committee will operate mainly through three sub-committees. The first of these will deal with Kenya, the second with Uganda, and the third with the Tanganyika Territory, Zanzibar, Nyasaland, and Northern Rhodesia.

label: text
text: Evidence was taken by Major C. Willson at the Central Magistracy this morning in a charge of assault preferred against a Chinese waiter of the Victoria Café, Des Voux Rond Central.

label: text
text: The complainant, Mr James Royston Stuart said that some dirty knives and forks were placed on the table when he went to have tillin along with his wife on Tuesday. Defendant took offences at a request to bring clean knives and attacked him with a knife in his hand. Complainant struck in self-defence and received a cut in his thumb.

label: text
text:
Defendant pleaded that he misunderstood what was wanted and on asking complainant to repeat the order he was struck in the face. Complainant then tried to hit him with a flower pot. He denied attacking complainant with a knife.
A witness called by defendant stated that he was in the inner room and saw the complainant pushing the defendant away. Defendant demonstrated and was struck in the cheek. Witness took a knife away from defendant's hand, and there was a clamour by the waiters for complainant's arrest.

label: text
text: Defendant explained that the complainant attempted to get away without paying for his meal.

label: text
text:
Complainant's wife stated in evidence that she did not actually see defendant pick up a knife nor did she see her husband strike defendant.
The Magistrate held that the charge had been proved and sentenced defendant to one month's hard labour.

label: text
text: The death of the Swedish Consul at Canton, Mr. C. Bertil Hellstrom, took place suddenly at his flat at No. 4, Banoo Buildings, Kowloon, late last night.

label: text
text: Mr. Hellatrom was in the Swedish Legation in Moscow from 1918 to 1918 and what he saw of developments in Canton since he took over the position he held at the time of his death led him to the belief that events would take place there similar to those which took place in Russia.

label: text
text: Speaking of what he saw whilst in Russia, Mr. Hellstrom stressed, at a public meeting in the City Hall on August 17, the dangers of applying the principles of Bolshevikism to China. The meeting, which was presided over by the Hon. Mr. P. H. Holyoak, was very well attended, some six hundred being present.

of Mr. Hellstrom are that he arrived in Hongkong yesterday by the afternoon boat from Canton and went straight to his flat. He was noticed going to his bathroom and as he did not put in an appearance for an hour or so the "boy" went to the bathroom and found it still locked. Receiving no answer to his knocks the "boy" reported the matter and it was decided to break open the thick window. When this was done, Mr. Hellstrom was found collapsed in a full bath, life being extinct.
The late Mr. Hellstrom was a single man, his home being Norrkjoping, Sweden, where he is survived by his mother and father. He was not appointed to Canton direct from the Legation at Moscow but was attached to the firm of Gilman and Co., Ltd., Hongkong, for a few years prior to his appointment as Swedish consul at Canton, a position he had held for just over a year.
At the time of going to press, the arrangements for fixing the time of the funeral had not been completed as they are contingent on the completion of a preliminary examination into the circumstances to the satisfaction of the Coroner. It had been hoped that the funeral would take place to day.
